title: Decision Trees
text: In this note, we check whether a decision tree can predict whether a teen carries a weapon to school.

Setup
Like before we load the packages necessary for the analysis.

library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(MLearnYRBSS)
library(janitor)
library(skimr)
library(vip)

analysis_split <- readRDS(here("models", "data", "analysis_split.rds"))

text:
Workflow

Recipe (preprocessing)
Trees don’t need fancy preprocessing: no step_normalize(), as trees only care about order, not scale; no step_dummy(), as rpart handles factor predictors natively; and imputation is still useful, since rpart can’t split on NA.

weapon_carry_recipe <- 
  recipe(formula = WeaponCarryingSchool ~ ., data = analysis_train) |>
  step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_impute_mean(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_zv(all_predictors())

Specification
We do the specification as follows.
As a result of the proportions of weapon-carrying being very unequal, when we set the rpart engine, we add the parameter parms = list(prior = c(0.5, 0.5)). This tells the rpart engine to treat each class equally, despite the proportional class imbalance.

cart_spec <-
    decision_tree(
        cost_complexity = tune(),
        tree_depth = tune(),
        min_n = tune()
    ) |>
    set_engine(
        "rpart",
        parms = list(prior = c(0.5, 0.5))
    ) |>
    set_mode("classification")

Run the tuning
Note for those following along that this part can be slow, as there are:

4 × 4 × 4 = 64 candidates
× 10 folds = 640 model fits

We’ll use doParallel to speed it up. Also, we use ROC AUC as the tuning metric — robust to class imbalance, and the same one we used for Lasso.

doParallel::registerDoParallel()

cart_tune <-
    cart_workflow |>
    tune_grid(
        resamples = analysis_folds,
        grid = tree_grid,
        metrics = metric_set(roc_auc),
        control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE)

Decision Trees
Logistic Regression
text:
Logistic regression is a statistical modeling approach used to estimate the relationship between one or more predictors and a binary outcome. In this analysis, the outcome of interest is whether an adolescent reported carrying a weapon at school. Because the outcome has two possible categories, logistic regression provides a natural framework for estimating how demographic, behavioral, social, and other measured characteristics are associated with the probability of weapon-carrying behavior.
Unlike ordinary linear regression, logistic regression does not model the outcome directly as a continuous value. Instead, it models the log-odds of the outcome and then converts those log-odds into a predicted probability between 0 and 1. This makes it possible to examine both the direction and magnitude of the association between each predictor and the likelihood of weapon carrying while accounting for the other predictors included in the model.
The analysis below uses the 2023 Youth Risk Behavior Survey (YRBS) analytic data and the tidymodels framework in R. The workflow includes data preprocessing, model specification and fitting, coefficient estimation, model evaluation, and visualization of the resulting odds ratios.

Model Overview
Logistic regression is appropriate when the dependent variable is binary, such as 0/1, Yes/No, or True/False. Here, WeaponCarryingSchool is treated as the binary response variable. The model estimates the probability that the outcome is in the event category given a set of predictor variables.
Each regression coefficient represents the estimated change in the log-odds of the outcome associated with a one-unit change in the predictor, holding the other variables constant. Because log-odds are difficult to interpret directly, the coefficients are exponentiated later in the analysis and reported as odds ratios. An odds ratio greater than 1 indicates higher estimated odds of weapon carrying, whereas an odds ratio less than 1 indicates lower estimated odds. An odds ratio close to 1 suggests little association with the outcome after accounting for the remaining predictors.
It is important to interpret these estimates as associations rather than causal effects. The YRBS data are observational, and the model cannot establish that any predictor causes an adolescent to carry a weapon at school.


Implementation
The analysis begins by loading the packages needed for data manipulation, model construction, evaluation, and file-path management. tidymodels supplies the modeling workflow, while tidyverse supports data manipulation and visualization. The dissertation data package and here are also loaded so that the analysis can access the prepared study data in a reproducible way.

library(tidymodels)
library(tidyverse)
library(dissertationData)
library(here)



Load the data
The analysis uses data objects previously prepared in the “Data and Research Question” section of this site. The full analytic dataset is loaded along with a training set, a test set, and resampling folds. Separating these objects allows the modeling process to distinguish between data used to estimate the model and data reserved for evaluation or resampling.
The training set is used below to fit the logistic regression model. The test set can be used for a more independent assessment of predictive performance, while the fold object supports cross-validation if resampling is incorporated into later model development.

analysis_data <- readRDS(here("models", "data", "analysis_data.rds"))
analysis_train <- readRDS(here("models", "data", "analysis_train.rds"))
analysis_test <- readRDS(here("models", "data", "analysis_test.rds"))
analysis_folds <- readRDS(here("models", "data", "analysis_folds.rds"))



Recipe
A recipe defines the preprocessing steps that will be applied before the model is fit. This is useful because it keeps data preparation tied directly to the modeling workflow and ensures that the same transformations can be reproduced consistently.
The recipe specifies WeaponCarryingSchool as the outcome and includes the remaining variables as predictors. Several preprocessing steps are then applied. Missing categorical values are imputed using the most common category, while missing numeric values are replaced with the corresponding mean. Predictors with zero variance are removed because they contain no information that can help distinguish between outcome categories. Finally, highly correlated numeric predictors are screened using a correlation threshold of 0.70. Removing one variable from strongly correlated pairs can reduce redundancy and improve the stability and interpretability of the fitted coefficients.

weapon_carry_recipe <- 
  recipe(formula = WeaponCarryingSchool ~ ., data = analysis_data) |>
  step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_impute_mean(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_zv(all_predictors()) |> 
  step_corr(all_numeric_predictors(), threshold = 0.7)

Model Specification
The model specification identifies the type of statistical model to be estimated. logistic_reg() defines a logistic regression model, and the classification mode indicates that the objective is to predict membership in one of two outcome categories. The glm engine uses R’s generalized linear modeling framework to estimate the model.
The primary advantage of logistic regression in this context is that the estimated coefficients can be converted directly to odds ratios and used to describe the adjusted association between each predictor and weapon carrying at school.

weapon_carry_spec <- 
  logistic_reg() %>% 
  set_mode("classification") %>% 
  set_engine("glm")

The fitted model coefficients are then converted into a tidy table. Setting exponentiate = TRUE transforms the coefficients from the log-odds scale to odds ratios, which are more intuitive to interpret. The output also reports 95% confidence intervals and p-values for each estimated association.
For a categorical predictor, the odds ratio compares the category shown with the model’s reference category. An odds ratio greater than 1 indicates higher adjusted odds of weapon carrying, while an odds ratio below 1 indicates lower adjusted odds. Confidence intervals provide information about the precision of each estimate. When a 95% confidence interval includes 1, the estimated association is not statistically distinguishable from no association at the conventional 0.05 level.
In the fitted model, eight of the ten substantive predictors have 95% confidence intervals that exclude 1. The confidence intervals for ParentSubstanceUse1 and ParentIncarceration1 include 1, corresponding to p-values of 0.151 and 0.575, respectively. The intercept is retained in the model output but is not treated as a substantive predictor and is omitted from the forest plot. The magnitude and direction of the individual associations are examined in greater detail below.

Model Evaluation
Model evaluation asks a different question from coefficient interpretation. The regression coefficients describe associations between individual predictors and the outcome, while predictive-performance measures assess how effectively the model distinguishes adolescents who reported weapon carrying at school from those who did not.
The fitted model is first used to generate predictions for the training data. The augmented output includes the observed outcome, the predicted class, and the estimated probability of each outcome category. These probabilities can then be used to evaluate discrimination across different classification thresholds.

weapon_pred <- 
  augment(mod_1, analysis_train) |> 
  select(WeaponCarryingSchool, .pred_class, .pred_1, .pred_0)

For each student, .pred_1 represents the estimated probability of reporting weapon carrying at school, while .pred_0 represents the estimated probability of not reporting weapon carrying. The .pred_class column converts these probabilities into a binary prediction using the classifier’s decision threshold. Because the outcome may be relatively uncommon, the continuous predicted probabilities are more informative for evaluating model performance than the resulting class labels. The upcoming ROC analysis therefore uses .pred_1 rather than .pred_class to evaluate how well the model distinguishes students who reported weapon carrying from those who did not.
Next, the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve summarizes the model’s ability to rank observations according to their predicted probability of the event. The curve compares sensitivity with the false-positive rate across all possible probability thresholds. A model with little discriminatory ability will produce a curve close to the diagonal reference line, while a model with stronger discrimination will bow farther toward the upper-left corner.
The corresponding area under the ROC curve, or AUC, can be interpreted as the probability that the model assigns a higher predicted risk to a randomly selected adolescent with the outcome than to a randomly selected adolescent without the outcome. Values closer to 1 indicate stronger discrimination, while a value near 0.5 indicates performance close to chance.
Because the ROC curve below is calculated on the training data, it primarily describes how well the fitted model separates the observations it was trained on. Predictive performance should generally also be evaluated on the held-out test set or through cross-validation to obtain a less optimistic estimate of how the model is likely to perform on new data.

roc_plot_training <- 
  weapon_pred |> 
  roc_curve(truth = WeaponCarryingSchool, .pred_1, event_level = "second") |> 
  autoplot()

roc_plot_training 








This ROC curve indicates that the fitted model has meaningful, though moderate, ability to discriminate between students who reported carrying a weapon at school and those who did not. The curve remains above the diagonal reference line, indicating performance better than random classification. The shape of the curve also demonstrates a substantial sensitivity-specificity tradeoff: achieving greater sensitivity requires accepting a considerable increase in the false-positive rate.


Visualizations
A forest plot provides a compact visual summary of the adjusted odds ratios and their 95% confidence intervals. Each point represents an estimated odds ratio for one predictor, and the horizontal line around the point represents its confidence interval. The vertical dashed line at an odds ratio of 1 represents no association with the outcome.
Predictors plotted to the right of 1 are associated with higher estimated odds of weapon carrying, whereas predictors plotted to the left of 1 are associated with lower estimated odds. The farther an estimate lies from 1, the larger the estimated association on the odds-ratio scale. Confidence intervals should be considered alongside the point estimates: wide intervals indicate greater uncertainty, and intervals that cross 1 do not clearly distinguish the estimated association from no association at the 95% confidence level.
The x-axis is displayed on a logarithmic scale. This is appropriate for odds ratios because values below and above 1 are then represented more symmetrically. For example, an odds ratio of 0.5 and an odds ratio of 2 represent effects of comparable magnitude in opposite directions on the log-odds scale.

tidy_model |> 
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = reorder(term, estimate))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), height = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Odds Ratio (log scale)",
    y = "Predictors",
    title = "Forest Plot of Logistic Regression Coefficients"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

Warning: `geom_errorbarh()` was deprecated in ggplot2 4.0.0.
ℹ Please use the `orientation` argument of `geom_errorbar()` instead.


`height` was translated to `width`.











Results and Interpretation
The fitted logistic regression identified several factors that were independently associated with weapon carrying at school after adjustment for the other predictors included in the model. The forest plot shows considerable variation in both the magnitude and precision of these associations.
Homelessness showed the strongest association with weapon carrying. The estimated odds ratio was approximately 3.2, indicating that adolescents in the category coded 1 for homelessness had more than three times the odds of reporting weapon carrying at school compared with the reference category, holding the other predictors constant. The 95% confidence interval remained well above 1, indicating a comparatively strong and statistically distinguishable association.
Several measures of exposure to violence or adversity were also strongly associated with weapon carrying. Being attacked in the neighborhood was associated with approximately twice the odds of weapon carrying, as was parental physical abuse. Both estimates had confidence intervals entirely above 1. Bullying and sexual abuse by an older person were associated with more moderate increases in the odds of weapon carrying, but their confidence intervals likewise remained above the null value of 1.
Parental monitoring also had an odds ratio substantially above 1. Because the direction of this association depends on how the variable was coded, the substantive interpretation should be made with reference to the original coding of the measure. If the category coded 1 represents lower parental monitoring, for example, the result would indicate that reduced monitoring is associated with greater odds of weapon carrying. This coding should be confirmed before assigning a substantive direction to the association.
Two predictors had odds ratios close enough to 1 that their 95% confidence intervals crossed the null value. Parent incarceration showed only a small positive estimated association, while parent substance use showed an estimated odds ratio below 1. In both cases, however, the confidence intervals included 1. These results therefore provide insufficient evidence of an independent association with weapon carrying after adjustment for the other predictors in this model.
At the other end of the distribution, school connectedness had one of the lowest odds ratios in the model, with its confidence interval entirely below 1. The category coded 1 was therefore associated with substantially lower odds of weapon carrying than the reference category. Unfair discipline at school also had an odds ratio below 1 with a confidence interval that appears to remain below 1. As with parental monitoring, however, the coding of these variables should be verified before describing them substantively as protective or risk factors. The statistical model establishes the direction of the association between the coded categories, not necessarily the direction implied by the variable’s name.
Taken together, the results suggest that experiences involving housing instability, interpersonal violence, and victimization are among the strongest correlates of adolescent weapon carrying in this model. Homelessness stands out in particular, while neighborhood violence, parental physical abuse, bullying, and sexual abuse also retain meaningful associations after simultaneous adjustment for the other included factors.
These estimates should be interpreted as conditional associations rather than causal effects. The analysis shows that these factors are associated with weapon carrying after adjustment for the other measured predictors, but it does not establish that any one factor causes weapon-carrying behavior. Unmeasured confounding, the coding and measurement of survey variables, self-report bias, and the observational nature of the YRBS data should all be considered when interpreting the findings.


Key Takeaways
The logistic regression framework allows the relationship between multiple predictors and adolescent weapon carrying at school to be examined simultaneously. The preprocessing recipe addresses missing data, removes predictors that contain no variation, and reduces redundancy among highly correlated numeric variables before model fitting.
The exponentiated model coefficients are interpreted as adjusted odds ratios. Values above 1 indicate higher odds of weapon carrying and values below 1 indicate lower odds, with 95% confidence intervals communicating the uncertainty around those estimates. The forest plot makes these relationships easier to compare visually and helps distinguish large, precise associations from estimates that are smaller or more uncertain.
The ROC analysis provides a separate assessment of the model’s ability to distinguish between adolescents who did and did not report weapon carrying at school. Because the ROC curve shown here is based on the training data, it should be viewed as an in-sample assessment. Evaluation with the held-out test data or cross-validation would provide stronger evidence about the model’s performance on new observations.
Taken together, the analysis is best used to identify and compare factors associated with weapon-carrying behavior and to assess how well those factors collectively discriminate the outcome. The results should not be interpreted as demonstrating that any individual predictor causes weapon carrying.

Workflow

Recipe
Our recipe is as follows:

weapon_recipe <-
    recipe(WeaponCarryingSchool ~ ., data = analysis_train) |>
    step_downsample(WeaponCarryingSchool, under_ratio = 1) |>
    step_zv(all_predictors()) |>
    step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
    step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
    step_impute_mean(all_numeric_predictors()) |>

title: Lasso Regression
text:
Lasso regression is a statistical model that combines linear/logistic regression with L1 regularization to perform both variable selection and regularization. The term “Lasso” stands for “Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator.” This method is particularly useful when dealing with datasets that have many predictors, as it helps to: - Reduce overfitting by penalizing large coefficients - Perform automatic feature selection by shrinking some coefficients to exactly zero - Handle multicollinearity by selecting only one variable from a group of highly correlated predictors
In this analysis, we’ll use Lasso regression to predict weapon carrying behavior in schools, demonstrating how this method can help identify the most important predictors while maintaining model interpretability.

title: Lasso Regression

Setting Up the Environment
First, we need to load the necessary packages for our analysis. We’ll use tidymodels for modeling, tidyverse for data manipulation, and here for consistent file paths.

title: Lasso Regression
text:
Results and Interpretation
The variable-importance ranking suggests that immediate instability and exposure to violence or victimization are the strongest predictors of adolescent weapon-carrying behavior. Homelessness stands out by a substantial margin as the most influential variable, followed by being attacked in the neighborhood and experiencing parental physical abuse. Parental monitoring also contributes meaningfully, while bullying and sexual abuse by an older person form a second tier of important predictors.
School-related factors, including unfair discipline and school connectedness, appear considerably less influential in the model, while parental substance use and especially parental incarceration contribute relatively little once the other predictors are taken into account.
One important qualification: variable importance measures predictive contribution, not direction or causation. This plot alone does not tell us whether a predictor increases or decreases the likelihood of weapon carrying. For example, the importance of parental monitoring could reflect either low monitoring as a risk factor or high monitoring as a protective factor, depending on how the variable was coded and how the model behaves.
Thus, weapon-carrying behavior was predicted most strongly by homelessness and direct exposure to violence or abuse. Homelessness was substantially more important than any other predictor, followed by neighborhood victimization and parental physical abuse. Parental monitoring, bullying, and sexual abuse also contributed meaningfully, whereas school-related factors, parental substance use, and parental incarceration had comparatively lower predictive importance. However, variable importance reflects predictive contribution and should not be interpreted as indicating either the direction of association or causation.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Documentation

Update URLs with 301 redirects. Most of them were HTTP to HTTPS redirects.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

R.utils::commandArgs() recognizes new --no-echo option in R (>= 4.0.0).

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

R.utils::getAbsolutePath("~/../Documents", expandTilde = TRUE) would adjust for .. before adjusting for ~ resulting in an incorrect path. Thanks to Dean Attali for reporting on this.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

wrap() for arrays used a list - not a numeric vector - to assign dimensions. This would produce an error in R (>= 4.0.0).
withSeed(..., seed = NULL) did not work for R (< 3.0.0).
fileAccess(..., mode = 2) would update .Random.seed.
fileAccess(path, mode = 2) could end up in an endless loop if the path folder contained all files of a, b, ..., z, A, B, ... Z.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

sourceDirectory() did not respect argument modifiedOnly. Thanks to Anton Krasikov for the report and the fix.
createLink() could produce a spurious warning on MS Windows.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Deprecated and Defunct

Previously defunct arrayIndex(), evalWithTimeout(), and resetWarnings() have been removed.
Assert$inherits() is defunct - use Assert$inheritsFrom() instead.
Argument substitute of withCapture() is defunct - use replace instead.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

createWindowsShortcut() gained argument mustWork.
When createLink() fails, the error message now also report on the methods attempted.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

displayCode(), commandArgs() and toCamelCase() used && and || on logical vectors that might not necessarily be of length one.
createWindowsShortcut() and createLink(method="windows-shortcut") failed to create Windows Shortcut links because filePath(..., expandLinks = "any") did not expand Windows Shortcut links. This bug was introduced in R.utils 1.34.0 (2014-10-07) due to a cut’n’paste mistake.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added nullcon() that returns a (binary) connection to the nullfile().

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Performance

readTable() no longer runs the garbage collector - was done so implicitly through an internal system.time() call without using gcFirst = FALSE.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

Rscript -e "R.utils::cmdArg(a=42L)" -a:=1:3 would set a to NA_integer_.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Deprecated and Defunct

evalWithTimeout() is now defunct. Use withTimeout() instead.
arrayIndex() is now defunct. Use base::arrayInd() instead.
Assert$inherits() is deprecated - renamed to Assert$inheritsFrom().
Removed deprecated and ignored argument reset of warnings() for Verbose.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Argument install of use() now defaults to option R.utils.use.install, which in turn defaults to environment variable R_R_UTILS_USE_INSTALL. If neither is set, the default is TRUE.
ROBUSTNESS: Now gcDLLs() runs the garbage collector before removing stray DLLs in order for any finalizers who rely on the DLL to be called before the DLL is removed.
loadObject() and loadToEnv() give more informative error message if an error occurs while reading from a file / connection.
All withNnn() functions gained argument substitute making it possible to pass an expression object, e.g. withTimeout(expr, subsitute = FALSE, ...). The exception is withCapture(), where, the now deprecated (see below), argument substitute means something else for legacy reasons.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

withTimeout() would produce a regular error but not a TimeoutException for timeouts reaching the total CPU time limit while it would work for those reaching the elapsed CPU time limit. Thanks to Alexej Gossmann at Tulane University for troubleshooting and provide a fix.
findSourceTraceback() could fail and give an obscure error when for instance the XML package was attached. It now tries a bit harder to locate the internal srcfile object.
Forgot to register S3 method [() for GenericSummary.
intToOct() would convert to hexadecimals.
intToBin() would output garbage for negative values.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Deprecated and Defunct

Argument substitute of withCapture() has been renamed to replace. Code that calls withCapture(..., substitute = ...) will still work, but the use of substitute is deprecated and will later become defunct. The purpose of this change of argument name is so that the meaning of substitute can be harmonized with the other withNnn() functions.
Deprecated evalWithTimeout(); use withTimeout() - the preferred name.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

withCapture(x <- 1L) would drop integer suffix L from the output when run in non-interactive mode.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Deprecated and Defunct

CLEANUP: Removed operator %<-% which was defunct since 2.4.0. An alternative is to use ditto of the future package.
CLEANUP: Made resetWarnings() defunct.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added strayDLLs() and gcDLLs() to identify and unload stray DLLs that was left behind by packages that have already been unloaded.
Added nullfile().
Now setThreshold() for Verbose accepts also logical values.
Argument absolutePath for Arguments$getReadablePathname() was renamed to absolute. For backward compatibililty, the old name will still work for some time.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Deprecated and Defunct

CLEANUP: Defunct %<-% in favor of %<-% in the future package.
CLEANUP: Deprecated arrayIndex(). arrayInd() in base (>= 2.11.0) provides the same functionality.

CODE REFACTORING:

Package now formally requires R (>= 2.14.0) released October 2011.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added hsize().
Added tmpfile() for creating temporary files with content that is deleted automatically by the garbage collector unless there is a reference to it.
ROBUSTNESS: Now compressFile() and decompressFile(), and therefore also functions such as gzip() and gunzip(), output atomically by writing to a temporary file which is only renamed when completed.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Deprecated and Defunct

CLEANUP: Deprecated %<-% in favor of %<-% in the future package.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Code Refactoring

Package now formally requires R (>= 2.14.0) released Oct 2011.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

loadObject() and saveObject() gained argument format in order to support also RDS files (in addition to XDR files). File formats XDR and RDS are supported. The default format is inferred from the filename extension. If this is not possible, then the XDR format is assumed (default; backward compatible).
mkdirs() gained arguments mustWork and maxTries.
seqToHumanReadable() gained argument tau.
R.utils::commandArgs() now also ackowledges argv set by the littler executable.
R.utils::commandArgs() recognizes more reserved command-line arguments, e.g. --debugger-args=N, --min-vsize=N, and --min-nsize=N.
ROBUSTNESS: Now writeDataFrame(..., sep, quote = FALSE) asserts that none of the columns contains the field separator sep, because then the written file would be corrupt/invalid.
ROBUSTNESS: Explicit import of all graphics, grDevices, stats and utils functions.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Documentation

Clarified in help for compressFile() et al. that these functions remove the input file by default after the output file is generated. Thanks to Ben Bond-Lamberty (Pacific Northwest National Laboratory) for pointing out this potential pitfall.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

seqToHumanReadable(c(1:2, 4:5)) gave "1-2, 4, 5".
withTimeout() did not work in non-English locales. Thanks to Arnaud Malapert at University Nice Sophia Antipolis for reporting on this.
GString ignored “simple” attributes, e.g. $[tolower]{y}. Thanks to Andre Mikulec for reporting on this.
downloadFile() via https://<user>:<pwd>@<domain>/ gave an error.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Deprecated and Defunct

CLEANUP: Deprecated resetWarnings().

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added compressPDF() to compress PDFs.
If, and only if, path is an existing directory, then copyFile(pathname, path) copies file pathname to the path directory (previously destination always had to be a file). Analogously, renameFile(pathname, path) moves file pathname (not a directory though) to destination directory path.
CLEANUP: createLink(..., skip = TRUE) would give a false warning if a proper link already existed and the target was elsewhere than the current directory.
INCONSISTENCY: captureOutput(..., collapse = "\n") did not drop newline of the last line as captureOutput(..., collapse = "\r") and any other collapse != "\n" strings. Added package tests.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

captureOutput(..., file = "foo.txt") gave an error.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

Arguments$getReadablePathname(NA, mustExist = FALSE) no longer gives an error with recent R devel (>= 2015-04-23) related to an update on how nchar() handles missing values. This bug affected only Windows.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Code Refactoring

ROBUSTNESS: Now nchar(..., type = "chars") is used internally for all file and directory names.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

R.utils no longer generates a warning if the R session is saved when R exits. Thanks to Jose Alquicira Hernandez for reporting on this.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

toCamelCase() with missing values would give an error in R devel (>= 2015-04-23) due to an update how nchar() handles missing values.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

ROBUSTNESS: Now %<-% evaluates the expression in a local() environment, and it assign to environments, e.g. env$a %<-% 1.
Added compressFile(), decompressFile() and isCompressedFile() methods, which gzip()/gunzip() and the new bzip2()/bunzip2() now use. Thanks to Peter Hickey for pushing for this.
Now eget() uses inherits = FALSE (was TRUE) and mode = "default" (was "any"), where "default" corresponds to the mode of argument default, unless it’s NULL when mode = "any" is used.
Now commandArgs(asValues = TRUE, adhoc = TRUE) interprets x:=1:10 such that x become the integer vector 1:10. Likewise, you can do x:=seq(1,3, by = 0.1) and x:=pi. To get the string "pi", use quotation marks, i.e. x:="pi", or just x=pi.
Added cmsg(), cout(), ccat(), cprintf(), cprint(), cstr(), cshow() for outputting to “console”, which is neither R stdout nor stderr and can therefor not be intercepted via capture.output(), sink() or similar. These functions are useful for outputting messages that requires user’s attention and are often followed by a prompt via readline(), which also cannot be captured.
Added mpager() which is a “pager” function compatible with file.show() that will display file contents on standard error.
Just like for listDirectory(), argument recursive of findFiles() can in addition to be FALSE (depth = 0) and TRUE (depth = +Inf), be any non-negative numeric number specifying how deeply the recursive search should be done.
On Windows, Arguments$getReadablePathname() now gives an informative warning if a pathname of length 256 or longer is used/generated, which are not supported on Windows.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Documentation

Fixed mistake in help("captureOutput"). Thanks to Mikko Korpela (Issue #4) for reporting on this.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

use(..., quietly = FALSE) no longer captures/buffers the output, which prevented it from displaying full prompt messages that required a user response. use(..., quietly = TRUE), which is the default, no longer tries to ask user of Windows and OS X if they wish to install from source if the binary is older.
Now the returned value of all withNnn() functions preserves the “visibility” of the eval():uated expression. Added package tests.
withCapture({}) no longer generates a warning.
Now isUrl(NA) returns FALSE (instead of NA).
seqToIntervals(integer(0)) gave error “object res not found”.
attachLocally() on an environment would remove the attached fields/variables from that environment.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Code Refactoring

ROBUSTNESS: Forgot to declare “default” warnings() as an S3 method.
R.utils::use() without arguments attaches R.utils.
ROBUSTNESS: Package test coverage is 66%.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Code Refactoring

Added URL and BugReports fields to DESCRIPTION.
Submitted to CRAN.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added shell.exec2(), which does a better job than shell.exec() in opening pathnames with forward slashes and files on mapped drives, which may or may not open depending software, e.g. Google Chrome fails to open the latter. Add options(browser = function(...) R.utils::shell.exec2(...)) to your ~/.Rprofile file to make browseURL() use this function instead of shell.exec(). This function is only useful on Windows.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

Now Arguments$getReadablePathname(file, path) ignores path if file specifies an absolute pathname.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Now countLines() automatically supports gzipped files as well. Thanks to Sarah Nelson at Dept of Biostatistics at University of Washington for the suggestion.
Now downloadFile("https://...") will use curl, and if not available wget, to download the file over the HTTPS protocol. Previously only wget was used. The curl software is available on more operating systems, include OS X, whereas wget sometimes needs a separate installation.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added argument unmap to filePath() for “following” paths that are on mapped Windows drives.
CLEANUP: use() would try temporarily set package repository options even when not needed. This could trigger unnecessary warnings for users who haven’t set a default CRAN mirror and using use() to load/attach an already installed package.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

New default for writeDataFrame() - argument col.names = !append. Also, if append = TRUE, header comments are only written if specified. Added package system test for writeDataFrame().

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

getAbsolutePath("/tmp", expandTilde = TRUE) returned "//tmp". This would in turn have implications on getRelativePath(), e.g. getRelativePath("/tmp/a", relativeTo = "/tmp") returned "../../tmp/a".

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added withSeed() and withSink().
ROBUSTNESS: Now withOptions() also resets all the options available upon entry even if no explicit options were specified. This covers the case when expr changes the options and/or adds new options, e.g. withOptions({ options(width = 10, foo = "new"); str(letter) }).

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

ROBUSTNESS: Arguments$getWritablePathname() could sometimes generate warning “file.remove(pathnameT) : cannot remove file ‘file…’, reason ‘Permission denied’.” Now it tries to remove that files several times before giving up.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

ROBUSTNESS: Now copyDirectory(), just as copyFile() already did, silently drops arguments copy.mode and copy.date for older R versions where base::file.copy() does not support them.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

mkdirs() could return “object ‘res’ not found” error.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

countLines() would not count the last line if it did not contain a newline. It would also give an error if the newline characters were only CR. This despite it was documented that both cases were supported. Added package system tests for them.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added mprint(), mcat(), mstr(), mshow() and mprintf() that work like the corresponding print(), cat(), etc., but output using message(), which in turn sends to standard error (instead of standard output). See also mout().
Added withLocale().
Now the test for target discrepancies by createLink(..., skip = TRUE) is more forgiving on Windows (by assuming a case-insensitive file system) before generating a warning.
Now useRepos(..., fallback = TRUE), and hence use(), will fallback to known/predefined CRAN repositories in case @CRAN@ is not set. If done, it will give an informative warning message.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

commandArgs() would drop command-line arguments with periods, hyphens, or underscores in their names, e.g. --src_file=x.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

withCapture({ if (T) 1 else 2 }) would give a parse error on “unexpected ‘else’”, because the internal deparsing puts the ‘else’ statement on a new line whenever an if-else statement is enclosed in an { … } expression. This problem is also described in R help thread “deparse() and the ‘else’ statement” by Yihui Xie on 2009-11-09 [http://tolstoy.newcastle.edu.au/R/e8/help/09/11/4204.html]. The workaround is to detect standalone ‘else’ statements and merge them with the previous line. Added package system test for this case.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

egsub() would return an invalid expression if the input had definitions of functions without arguments, e.g. egsub("x", "x", substitute(y <- function() 0)), which would throw “Error: badly formed function expression” if deparsed/printed. Added package test for this.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Now egsub() also works with functions, in case it substitutes on the body of the function.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Documentation

Added clarification to help("withTimeout") on the limitations of the function and when it is/is not possible to interrupt a function via timeouts.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Software Quality

Made the package test on absolute and relative paths less conservative, because it gave an error on Windows systems that have set R_USER to a Cygwin-flavored directory, which causes normalizePath("~") to return a non-existing directory. Thanks Uwe Ligges (CRAN) for reporting on this.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

filePath("./././././") now returns "." (was ""). Added package system tests for filePath().

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added support for substitution of expressions in withCapture() based on regular expressions utilizing new egsub().
Added egsub(), which is gsub() for expressions with some bells and whistles.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Now downloadFile() “adjusts” the output filename by decoding URL encoded characters, e.g. Hello%20world.txt becomes Hello world.txt. Also, unsafe filename characters (:, *, \) are encoded, e.g. How_to:_RSP.txt becomes How_to%3A_RSP.txt.
Added argument adjust to Arguments$getReadablePathname(). When adjust = "url" it decodes and encodes the filename the same way as downloadFile() now adjusts it (see above).

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added captureOutput() which is much faster than capture.output() for large outputs. withCapture() utilizes this now. Added package system tests for both functions.
use() now installs missing packages from all set repositories (as before) and uses the mainstream (CRAN and Bioconductor) ones as fall backs.
Added withRepos() for installing/updating packages using a set of temporarily set repositories. It is possible to specify repositories by names, which are then selected from a set of known repositories, e.g. withRepos(install.packages("edgeR"), repos = "[[BioC]]").
Added withOptions() for evaluating an expression with a set of options temporarily set.
Renamed evalCapture() to withCapture() and evalWithTimeout() and withTimeout(). The old name is kept for backward compatibility, but will eventually be deprecated.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Now use("<repos>::<pkg>") will detect when a repository is unknown and give an informative error message on how to update option repos.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added assignment operator %<-% for delayed assignments.
Added option evalCapture/newline.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added argument xtrim to draw() for density object.
CLEANUP: createLink(..., skip = TRUE) no longer warns if the link file was skipped. Now it only warns if the skipped link file links to a different file than the intended target file.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Code Refactoring

CLEANUP: Dropping :: in calls where possible.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added argument newline to evalCapture().

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added argument substitute to evalCapture() for substituting symbols “on the fly” in the expression before it is evaluated.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added argument modifiedOnly to sourceDirectory(), which was previously passed via ... to sourceTo(), and it now defaults to TRUE.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

use() would not install package dependencies.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added argument max.deparse.length to evalCapture().

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Now evalCapture() utilizes deparse() to get the source code and acknowledges options deparse.cutoff to control the code wrapping. Previously capture.output(print()) was used.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

WORKAROUND: moveInSearchPath() redirects any messages to stderr that base::attach() sent to stdout. UPDATE: This attach() issue has been fixed in R 3.1.0 patched.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Vectorized detachPackage(), getAbsolutePath(), getRelativePath(), isAbsolutePath(), isDirectory(), isFile(), isOpen(), isPackageInstalled(), touchFile() and toUrl(). Added package system tests for several of them.
For backward compatibility, getAbsolutePath(), getRelativePath(), isAbsolutePath(), isFile(), and isDirectory() treats an empty vector of path/pathnames equal to ".". However, in a future version, empty results will returned by these too.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

toCamelCase(character(0L)) gave an error.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

str() and summary() for Verbose did not acknowledge argument level.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Documentation

Added a help section on privileges required on Windows in order for createLink() to work.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

ROBUSTNESS: Added a package redundancy test for a bug occurring in R.oo (< 1.18.0) causing R to core dump (with "Error: SET_VECTOR_ELT() can only be applied to alist, not ainteger") or gives an error (with “Error: not a weak reference”) under certain conditions when a registered finalizer tried to reload R.oo if it was unloaded. This occurred only on R prior to R 3.0.2 patched (2014-02-21 r65057). Also, the methods package needs to be attached, so it is still not clear what is the true cause of the bug. In R.oo (>= 1.18.0) this bug is avoided.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

Although eget(K = 2, cmdArgs = TRUE) would use command-line argument K = 1 as the default (instead of K = 2), calling eget("K", 2, cmdArgs = TRUE) would not.
commandArgs(excludeReserved = TRUE) failed to drop reserved arguments of type --<key>=<value>, e.g. --encoding=ASCII.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added trial version of the CmdArgsFunction class.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added cmdArgsCall() for easy calling of functions from the command line, e.g. Rscript -e R.utils::cmdArgsCall(rnorm) n=4.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

doCall() gained argument envir, which also means that the new behavior is to evaluate the call within the calling frame. Also, doCall() now accepts call a function object in addition to a name of a function.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added argument unique to cmdArgs().
Now commandArgs(asValues = TRUE) returns no-named arguments as a list element with the argument as the value and with a "" name. For instance, in the past one would get list(R = NA, a = "1", noname = NA), whereas now one gets list("R", a = "1", "noname").

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Bug Fixes

Now attachLocally() no longer tries to attach elements with an empty name, e.g. list(a = 1, 2). Previously it gave an error. Added a package system test for attachLocally().

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

CONSISTENCY: Now createLink(..., method = "windows-shortcut") returns the path/pathname to the link (and not the target) just like it does for the other types of file links. By link we here mean the path/pathname without the *.lnk extension.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
Software Quality

ROBUSTNESS: Added package system tests for createLink().

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Now Arguments$getCharacters() preserves attributes. Also, made argument useNames defaults to TRUE.
Added [() for GenericSummary.

title: Version 2.13.0 [2025-02-24]
text:
New Features

Added argument what to Sys.readlink2(), where what = "corrected" makes sure to return the proper target path (not just the one relative to where the link lives).

title: Version 1.8.2 [2022-06-13]
text: Very old, deprecated argument enforceRCC for setGenericS3() and setMethodS3() is now defunct in favor of argument validators.

title: Version 1.8.2 [2022-06-13]
text: Very old, deprecated argument enforceRCC for setGenericS3() and setMethodS3() is now defunct in favor of argument validators.

title: Version 1.8.2 [2022-06-13]
text:
Bug Fixes

R.methodsS3 would produce “Warning: partial match of ‘Date’ to ‘Date/Publication’” when attached if options(warnPartialMatchDollar = TRUE).

title: Version 1.8.2 [2022-06-13]
text:
Significant Changes

Now setGenericS3() produces an error if it can not turn an existing function into a “default” function and create a new generic function. Previously, it produced a warning.

title: Version 1.8.2 [2022-06-13]
text:
New Features

Now setGenericS3() sets the S3class attribute on any “default” methods it creates, if any.
Add internal function R.methodsS3:::makeNamespace(pkg) for producing S3method() statements to be put in a package’s NAMESPACE file.

title: Version 1.8.2 [2022-06-13]
text:
Code Quality

Now formally suggesting codetools.

title: Version 1.8.2 [2022-06-13]
text:
Bug Fixes

title: EEG Seminar Notes
text:
Setting Up Data
Though they use the data at alexenge/erpcore, we will use the data from eegverse/erpcore, as the former does not seem to exist anymore on GitHub.

pak::pak("eegverse/erpcore")

library(erpcore)
library(here)    # For general handling of local data files

Moreover, we will only be using data from the N170 experiment, which showed that subjects who were hooked up to EEGs and were tasked with viewing faces elicited different responses than when they were tasked to view cars.

data_dir <- here("eegs", "data/n170") # for me, all of my files are in ./eegs/ 
dir.create(data_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# This function downloads all n170 data to `data_dir`
get_erpcore(
  component = "n170",
  dest_path = data_dir,
  type = "bids",          # we only want data in BIDS format
  subjects = "sub-001",   # limit our subjects  to just 001 for now
  conflicts = "overwrite"
)

title: EEG Seminar Notes
text:
Preprocessing
For preprocessing, we first load eegUtils, a package for working with EEG data.

pak::pak("craddm/eegUtils")

library(eegUtils)

The downloaded ERP CORE data is in data/n170, as we specified in the setup section. The data is in BIDS format; though the seminar notes say the subjects are each in their respective sub-XXX/egg directory, on my end the file structure looks like {subject-number}/{subject-number}_N170.set.
So, we retrieve this .set file for subject 1:

bids_dir <- here("eegs", "data/n170")
set_file <- here(bids_dir, "1/1_N170.set")
file.exists(set_file)

[1] TRUE


eegUtils has functions for importing raw EEG data from various file formats into R, including the .set format used by ERP CORE.

# Needed these packages for `import_set` to work
pak::pak("R.matlab", "hdf5r") 


dat_raw <- import_set(set_file)

The data we actually care about is in the dat_raw$signals data frame. Here, each row is one sample (time point), each column is one channel (EEG electrode), and each value is the EEG voltage (in microvolts; µV) measured at this time sample and channel.

Viewing Data
We can visually check the data at multiple steps using the browse_data function. This will open a site we can open either on our browser or in the “Viewer” tab on the right-hand side of RStudio from which we can interactively inspect the data. We can use the function as is by calling browse_data on our dat_raw, i.e. browse_data(dat_raw), or we can manually specify which time steps we want to see as follows:

time_lim <- c(300, 305)
browse_data(dat_raw, time_lim, baseline = time_lim)

Note that unlike in the seminar example, the interactive example does not give a legend showing which colors indicate which channel. Below is the example image given in the seminar:

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

Now the R.matlab Package object is also available when the package is only loaded (but not attached).
ROBUSTNESS: Added package system test asserting that readMat() can be called without attaching the package.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

Package now only imports R.oo (no longer attaches it). Also, the package now imports R.utils (used to suggest and attach it when needed). These updates make the package more “silent”.
Dropped obsolete autoload():s.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

Now the ‘INTERNAL ERROR’ message readMat() throws on failed decompression also includes the first and last bytes of the data block that it tried to decompress. This will further help troubleshooting.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

ROBUSTNESS: Forgot to import R.methodsS3::appendVarArgs().

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]

Code Refactoring

ROBUSTNESS: Added one explicit import from the utils package.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

CONSISTENCY: Added argument drop to readMat() to control how singleton dimensions of for instance nested lists are dropped or not. The defaults are now such that R.matlab v2.0.4 is consistent with R.matlab v1.7.1 (R.matlab v2.0.0-2.0.3 were not). Thanks to Claudia Beleites at IPHT Jena, Germany for reporting on this.
Bumped package dependencies.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

readMat() would produce an error when parsing an empty mxCHAR_CLASS matrix with a 0x0 dimension. It is not clear whether this is a valid MAT v5 structure or not, but I`ve added a workaround. Thanks Claudia Beleites at IPHT Jena, Germany for reporting on this.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Documentation

Added section of v7.3 MAT files to help("readMat").

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

Now the ‘INTERNAL ERROR’ message that people forward to the package maintainer also includes the version of the R.matlab package.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Documentation

Updated all documentation and messages to use MATLAB instead of Matlab.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

Bumped package dependencies.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Significant Changes

SPEEDUP: Made readMat() significant faster. More than 15x speedup(!) is observed on MAT files with many small structures. This was achieved by (i) dramatically decreasing the amount of memory allocation and garbage collection needed by the internal raw buffer mechanism, by (ii) dropping an internal rm() calls that was called very often, as well as by (iii) minimizing the number of times local functions and objects are created.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

Now readMat() also accepts a raw vector as input.
Now readMat() no longer generates warnings reporting on “In readBin( con = rawBufferT, what = what, size = size, n = n, signed = signed, : ‘signed = FALSE’ is only valid for integers of sizes 1 and 2.”

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Documentation

Restructured help("readMat"). Added a section on ‘Speed performance’.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Documentation

Now all Rd \usage{} lines are at most 90 characters long.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

readMat() now support reading 64-bit integers [array type (class) mxINT64_CLASS and mxUINT64_CLASS] on machines/versions of R with .Machine$sizeof.long >= 8 or .Machine$sizeof.longlong >= 8.
Package utilizes new startupMessage() of R.oo.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]

Nearly all S3 methods are now declared properly in the namespace.

Updated the help usage section for all static methods.

Bumped up package dependencies.

Code Refactoring

Updated package dependencies.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

readMat() could not read sparse matrices containing logical values, only numerics. This was because the logical bit in the Array Flags was not utilized by readMat(), which in turn was because the file format documentation is rather vague on how to use that bit. This means that readMat() now represents sparse logical matrices using logical values, except when sparseMatrixClass = "SparseM", because SparseM matrices can only hold numeric values. Thanks to Irtisha Sinhg at Cornell University for reporting on this.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

It is now possible to specify the decompression method for readMat().
Now readMat() decompression error messages are more informative.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

Package now only imports R.methodsS3.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

The Rcompression update in v1.5.5 introduced a bug, causing the loading of that package to fail.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

readMat(..., verbose = -111) gave an error on object zraw not being found.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Deprecated and Defunct

Removed Rcompression from set of “Suggests” packages, because since R v2.10.0 (Oct 2009) we can use memDecompress() of the base package instead. However, just in case someone is still running older versions of R, readMat() does indeed still look for Rcompression as a fallback.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

Removed all internal copies of base functions that have .Internal() calls.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Documentation

Added a section to help(Matlab) on how to connect through firewalls. Thanks Bas de Regt at University of Adelaide for the suggestion.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

Fixed an R CMD check NOTE that would show up in R v2.15.0 devel.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

The version 1.5.0 that was submitted to CRAN did not include the adjustments for startup messages. Thus, resubmitting this one to CRAN.
Updated dependencies on R and packages.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

GENERALIZATION: Now readMat() utilizes base::memDecompress() to uncompress compressed data structures, unless running R v2.9.x or before, in case Rcompression::uncompress() is used, iff installed. R v2.10.0 was released October 2009. Thanks Stephen Eglen at University of Cambridge for reminding me about memDecompress().
CLEANUP: Now using packageStartupMessage() instead of cat().

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

Added a namespace to the package, which will be more or less a requirement in the next major release of R.
CLEANUP: Now all references to the Rcompression package is within the local uncompress() function of readMat(). This makes the code more modular making it easier to implement alternatives to Rcompression::uncompress().

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Documentation

Added an example of verbose output to example(readMat).

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

Now using argument imaginary (not partial imag) in calls to complex().

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

Now writeMat() gives an error if duplicated object names are used, e.g. writeMat(..., A = 1, B = 2, A = 3).
Now writeMat() gives an error, not a warning, if there are non-named objects.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

The test for non-named objects to writeMat() did not work correctly. Thanks Claudia Beleites for the report.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

ROBUSTNESS: Although readMat() can read non-named objects, in MATLAB it is only the load() function call that can read it but not the plain ‘load’ call. Because of this, writeMat() will now give a warning if it detects non-named objects. For instance, in writeMat("foo.mat", x = a, y) the object a is named (as x) whereas y is not. To name the objects and avoid the warning, use writeMat("foo.mat", x = a, y = y). Thanks Claudia Beleites at University of Trieste for reporting on this.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Documentation

Clarified in the help of writeMat() that it can only write ‘uncompressed’ MAT files.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Documentation

Clarified and corrected some sentences in help(Matlab).
Added MATLAB 7.11.0.584 (R2010b) to the list of confirmed version that are compatible with R.matlab.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

The MatlabServer.m script incorrectly referred to the InputStreamByteWrapper class as java.io.InputStreamByteWrapper. This hopefully solves previously reports on obtaining “??? Undefined variable”java” or class “java.io.InputStreamByteWrapper”. Error in ==> MatlabServer at 262 reader = java.io.InputStreamByteWrapper(4096);“. This bug was introduced in R.matlab v1.2.5 (2009-08-25). Thanks Kenvor Cothey at GMO LCC for the report.R.utils

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

readMat() would throw an exception on “Error in dim(matrix) <- dimensionsArray$dim : dims [product 1] do not match the length of object [0]” in rare cases related to empty strings. Not sure if those cases are legal, but added an ad hoc workaround for them. Thanks Claude Flene at University of Turku for reporting this.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

Now the MatlabServer script reports it’s version when started.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Documentation

Removed some minor ambiguities in help(Matlab) and updated example(Matlab) with some more troubleshooting statements.
Added MATLAB 7.4.0 (R2007a), 7.7.0.471 (R2008b), and 7.10.0.499 (R2010a) to the list of confirmed version that are compatible with R.matlab. Thanks Ajay Tripathy at UC Berkeley and Marco Colombo at University of Edinburgh for reporting this.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

Now MatlabServer.m saves variables using the function form, i.e. save(). This solves the problem of having single quotation marks in the pathname. Thanks Michael Q. Fan at NC State University for reporting this problem.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Documentation

Minor update to argument fixNames of help(readMat). Thanks Stephen Eglen (University of Cambridge) for the suggestion.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

GENERALIZATION: Now readMat() can read also nested miMATRIX structures. Issue reported by Jonathan Chard at Mango Solutions, UK.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

MEMORY OPTIMIZATION: For very large compressed data objects, there would not be enough memory to allocate the internal buffer resulting in an error. Before this buffer was initiated to be 10 times the size of the compressed data. If that fails, now readMat() tries smaller and smaller initial buffers, before giving in up. Also, it now starts with a buffer 3 (not 10) times the compressed size. Thanks to Michael Sumner for the report.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

The MATLAB server script (MatlabServer.m) gave the error “Undefined function or method ServerSocket for input arguments of type double.”, when launching it via Matlab$startServer(). It seems like import java.net.*, etc. does not work. A workaround is to specify the full path for all Java classes, e.g. java.net.ServerSocket. Thanks Nicolas Stadler for the report.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

If onWrite == NULL, then there is no longer an outer two-pass scan for figuring out the size of MAT structure. However, instead each internal writeDataElement() has to do a two-pass scan in order to figure out the number of bytes before writing each element.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

Arrays with more than two dimension would be written as vectors. Thanks Minho Chae for the report.
From v1.2.2, writeMat() would generate corrupt MAT files. Reverted writeMat() back to v1.2.1 and updated as above.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Documentation

Updated example(readMat) so that it gives no error if the optional Rcompression package is not installed.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

Now the first pass in writeMat() that counts the number of bytes to be written is skipped if argument onWrite is not given. This means that writing to file, which is the most common use case, will no longer involve the counting. Thank to Adam Grossman at Stanford University for suggesting the modification and providing initial code. He reports a substantial speedup in writing large files (38 MB file).

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

Removed internal debugging/asserting code.
Renamed the HISTORY file to NEWS.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

In readMat()/writeMat() we use an internal character vector to represent the 8-bit ASCII character set. However, in R one cannot represent ASCII 0x00 - it resolves to an empty string, and from R v2.8.0 we will get a warning if we try. For now, we have replaced the ASCII for 0x00 with the empty string (unless before R v2.6.0). We might want to move away from using this ASCII vector for intToChar()/charToInt() and instead make use of intToUtf8()/utf8ToInt() or alternatively just rawToChar()/charToRaw().

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

Added support for reading compressed MAT files. It requires that the Rcompression package (Omegahat.org) is available.
Added support for also returning sparse matrices according to the representations given by either the Matrix or the SparseM package.
Added simple UTF-* string support. Conversion should be accurate when the R installation supports iconv.
Added mat-files/StructWithSparseMatrix-v4.mat from JR.
Credits for all of the above new feature goes to Jason Riedy at the Computer Science Dept, UC Berkeley. Thanks also to Duncan Temple-Lang at UC Davis for the Rcompression package.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

Added a “hint” to error message “Tag type not supported: miCOMPRESSED” to clarify that readMat() does not support compressed MAT files.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

Update so that package passes R CMD check on R v2.5.0.
Replaced Sys.putenv() with new Sys.setenv() (to be deprecated in R v2.5.0).

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

Now open() throws an error if connection to MATLAB failed (before FALSE was returned).
Extended the accepted range of ports to [1023,66535].

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Documentation

Added more details on available options in setOption() and how to avoid timeouts.
The example in help(Matlab) is now using default values for host and port making the example less confusing.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

When the port for the MATLAB server (MATLABSERVER_PORT) was out of range, a MATLAB syntax error occurred, i.e ‘… Line: 109 Column: 45 “)” expected, “identifier” found.’ Thanks Alexander Nervedi for the report.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

Added argument port to Matlab$startServer(..., port = NULL) to start the MATLAB server such that it listens to another port than the default 9999. Internally the server first tries to obtain the port number by environment variable MATLABSERVER_PORT. This feature was requested by Wang Yu at Iowa State University.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Documentation

Another version has been added to the list of MATLAB versions that are confirmed to work with R.matlab. See ?Matlab.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

If using the Matlab class, the package requires the R.utils where the classes Java and Verbose was moved. The methods for dealing with user options in the Matlab class are provided by the Options class also in R.utils. Similarly, if verbose != FALSE in readMat() or writeMat(), then the R.utils package is required.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

Forgot to “implement” miSINGLE, i.e. to set knownTypes and knownWhats for this. Thanks to Craig Aumann for the report.
readMat() did not read ‘complex’ matrices in MAT v5 correctly. Thanks to Chris Sims for the report.
readMat() did not read ‘text’ matrices in MAT v4 correctly. Thanks to Chris Sims, Princeton University, for the patch.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

Added support for user-defined options to Matlab objects via methods setOption() and getOption(). Current supported options are "readResult/maxTries" and "readResult/interval" to provide a “workaround” for the problem with timeout errors in evaluate(). Thanks Thomas Romary, France, for (re-)reporting on this problem.
Added class Options. This will probably move to another package whenever it becomes stable and widely used.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

Now MATLAB struct`s are read into an R structure.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

Replaces package directory misc/ with two new directories mat-files/ and externals/.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

Reading empty struct:s (and cells) tried to read one field because seq(0) and not seq(length = 0) was used. Updated all occurrences of this problem.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Documentation

Minor additions to help pages.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

readMat() failed to read some MATLAB struct`s because of a parsing error.
Internally in readMat() - in readMat5DataStructure() it might be data readTag() returns a tag referring to a data block of zero length (nbrOfBytes == 0). Now list(NULL) is returned in this case.
The MatlabServer script did (indeed) not work with MATLAB v7; a wrong version was included. Thanks Patrick Drechsler, University of Wuerzburg for reporting the above two problems.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

Updated the MatlabServer.m script to automatically set the Java classpath for MATLAB v7 and higher. This will assure that InputStreamByteWrapper.class is found as long as it is in the same directory as the *.m script. Thanks Yichun Wei at University of Southern California for suggesting this and also for suggesting additional help instructions.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Documentation

Added a Wishlist and an Acknowledgements section to “about”.
Added more information on how to start the MATLAB server.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Documentation

Updated the Matlab example to be more explicit about problems with Matlab$startServer() and MATLAB v7.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

Added autoload("hasVarArgs") to R/000.R.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

Package now passes R CMD check on R v2.1.0 devel without warnings.
Added appendVarArgs = TRUE to setMethodS3(), which specifies that ... should be added, if missing.
Add argument ... to all methods to make it even more consistent with any generic function. This is also done for a few methods in R base packages.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

readMat() would not read non-signed bytes correctly.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

Package passes R CMD check on R v2.1.0 devel too.
Moved the Java class from R.io to this package, since it is currently only used here. It is used for reading and writing Java bytes, ints and (UTF) strings when communicating with MATLAB.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

Added a setVerbose() method to the Matlab class, which allows the user to get details at various levels of the MATLAB process.
Added support for reading sparse matrices. Sparse matrices are expanded to regular matrices, which means that some may be too large to be loaded.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

WORKAROUND: It sometimes happens that the reply from MATLAB is not transferred “quick enough” and even if the connection should block we receive NULL giving an error. The workaround for now is to try to read the answer again. The symptom was that an error in readResult() complain about “if (answer == 0)” where answer was of length 0.
The header of MAT v4 files was not parsed correctly, which made MAT v4 files unrecognized and assumed to be MAT v5 files which in turn could not be read.
Used "sparce" instead of "sparse" in MOPT[4] tag (MAT v4), which most likely would generate an error for such structure.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

Introduced a bug that made files written with big endian not to work. The reason was that <- was used instead of <<- in one new method. I do not like <<-, but that is how it works.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

Created an readMat() that can read both MAT v4 and MAT v5 files. The MAT v4 reader was kindly provided by Andy Jacobson at the Princeton University.
writeMat() was created for consistency, but it does only support MAT v5.
Note that I have now chosen to rename readMAT() and writeMAT() to readMat() and writeMat(), respectively. This is in line with the RCC, cf. readHtml() instead of readHTML(). If you really need readMAT() and writeMAT() you can easily write your own wrappers.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

I forgot to remove some debug code that outputs information about the Description comment every time a MAT file is read. Removed.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

Now require(R.io) is loaded with the package and not when the first MATLAB client/server method is called. The former approach was a bit annoying.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

The MATLAB client/server implementation was broken due to bugs introduced in the Java class of the R.io package. Correcting these bugs made the MATLAB part work again.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Documentation

Made all methods use \keyword{internal}.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Bug Fixes

readMAT() would not work because getBits() previously in package R.oo was removed. getBits() is now added as a local function inside readMAT().

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
Code Refactoring

Upgraded to make use of Rx.oo.

title: Version 3.7.0 [2022-08-25]
text:
New Features

Initial methods are readMAT() and writeMAT() for reading and writing MATLAB MAT file structures.
Initial class is Matlab, which provides static methods for communicating with the running MATLAB server.
Package created.

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text: Rdoc$compile() would produce Error in strsplit(x, as.character(split), fixed, perl, useBytes) for any @see tag of format <pkg>::<object>.

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text: Rdoc$compile() would produce Error in strsplit(x, as.character(split), fixed, perl, useBytes) for any @see tag of format <pkg>::<object>.

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text:
Significant Changes

getMethods() is an R.oo generic in R (>= 4.5.0), whereas in versions before that it is n methods generic. This is because methods::getMethods() is being deprecated in base R.

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text:
Significant Changes

The hashCode(s) implementation for strings was rewritten to avoid integer overflow (see below bug fix). As a consequence, the computed hash is no longer the same for some strings.

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text:
Documentation

Fixed a few small mistakes in the help pages.

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text:
Bug Fixes

hashCode(s) could return NA, due to integer overflow, for strings with more than 13-15 symbols, e.g. hashCode("abcdefghijklmno") resulted in a missing value and a warning.

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text:
New Features

Now showNews() for Package recognizes ‘NEWS.md’ files too.

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text:
Bug Fixes

Rdoc no longer injects a dummy \emph{} at the end of @howtocite sections, because it now triggers an R CMD check --as-cran NOTE. The workaround was used to workaround an R CMD check false positive way back in 2004, which has since been fixed.

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text:
New Features

Added $<- and [[<- for Object to the list of S3 methods that tries to ignore objects of class Object that are of the kind that R.oo creates. This fixes conflicts with Object objects that the arrow package produces, which are non-R.oo objects. Other S3 Object methods already do this since R.oo 1.20.0 to workaround similar issues with the rJava package.

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text:
Bug Fixes

getDate() for Package returned NA because it was looking for DESCRIPTION field Date, which has been renamed to Date/Publication.

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text:
Significant Changes

Exporting generic throw(), which previously was a re-export of ditto from R.methodsS3. This change prevents the message “Registered S3 method overwritten by ‘R.oo’: … throw.default R.methodsS3” from appearing when the R.oo package is loaded (directly or indirectly).

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text:
Deprecated and Defunct

Removed defunct method gc() for Object. Use clearCache(..., gc = TRUE).

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text:
CRAN Policy

Don’t test example(getBundle.Package) because they may take more than 5 seconds when run on CRAN where installed.packages() will take a long time due to many thousands of packages.

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text:
New Features

Now generic function clone() is always created. This avoids the recurring issues where the creation of generic R.oo::clone() was skipped if another clone() generic already existed during package installation from source. This would in turn cause for instance the R.utils package to fail during loading (R.utils Issue #29). Thanks to Matt Dowle for reporting on this and insisting on a fix.

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text:
Deprecated and Defunct

Removed previously defunct update() for Package; use update.packages().
Removed previously defunct registerFinalizer() for Object.
Previous deprecated gc() for Object is now defunct; use clearCache(..., gc = TRUE) instead.

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text:
Bug Fixes

Method dispatching of [[<- for Object and BasicObject failed when running R CMD check in R-devel (>= 3.6.0) with environment variables _R_S3_METHOD_LOOKUP_BASEENV_AFTER_GLOBALENV and _R_S3_METHOD_LOOKUP_USE_TOPENV_AS_DEFENV both set to TRUE.

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text:
New Features

Now TAB-completion works on elements of Object, BasicObject, and Class.
Now getElement() works also for Object, Class, and BasicObject.
[[() for Object, Class and BasicObject gained argument exact, but exact = FALSE is currently ignored and treated as exact = TRUE.

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text:
Significant Changes

Package requires R (>= 2.13.0) (April 2011), because R.methodsS3 effectively requires that version.

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text:
New Features

Some S3 methods for R.oo classes Object and Exception would interfere with ditto for rJava objects that had class attributes containing "Object" and "Exception". Although these classes have the same name, and therefore are in conflict, they represent completely different classes. For methods where conflicts have been identified, the R.oo implementations will try to detect the conflict and call the next method instead.
Now print() and startupMessage() for Package report on package date only if date exists.

title: Version 1.27.1 [2025-05-02]
text:
Software Quality
